messages.subject: AW: CMR model with survival constrained by age (and environmental covariates)
parts:
Hi Sarah,

 

To be able to use a different covariate for each age class, you can construct a matrix with your covariates, where the columns refer to years and the rows to the covariates. Row 1 may then be the particular covariate for age 1, row 2 that of age 2, aso. Assuming that your matrix is named X, you would then use the following line of code in your model:

 

       logit(phi[i,t]) <- alpha[age[i,t]] + eps[age[i,t],t] + beta[age[i,t]] * X[age[i,t],t]

Best wishes

 

Michael

Betreff: CMR model with survival constrained by age (and environmental covariates)

 

Hello everyone,

 

I have what I think is more of a coding question, but it's something I've been banging my head against a wall about for awhile now so I thought I'd just ask. I'm following example 7.7 in "Bayesian population analysis using WinBUGS" along with the example in the recent " Zero-inflated count distributions for capture–mark– reencounter data" from Riecke et al. (2022). 

 

I am currently trying to figure out how I can constrain survival differently for juveniles and adults. I'm currently using an age matrix with nested indexing to account for the age structure, but I feel like this is causing problems when trying to incorporate different environemtnal covariates for the different age groups (but appears necessary for the curent CMR model structure). Currently I have the model set up to include random temporal effects,  but I'd like to eventually be able to include different environmental covariates for the different age groups (with juveniles being ages 0-3 and adults being aged 4+). I'm using only known-aged individuals in which exact age at marking is know. Any thoughts or suggestions about how to accomplish this would be grealty appreciated. I have the feeling it's an easy fix, I just can't seem to find to solution. Below I have pasted the pertinent parts of my code, happy to share some data if that would be helpful too. Cheers!

 

 

################ SELECTED CODE ################################

 

#Create age matrix covariate for known aged individuals
# Age 4 = average age of return, using this as break for juveniles/adults

# Juveniles ages 0-3, adults ages 4+


recode_ch <- function(ch, f){
  z <- ch
  for (i in 1:nrow(ch)) {
    for (j in 1:ncol(ch)) {
      if (j < (f[i])){z[i,j] <- NA}
      if (j == (f[i])){z[i,j] <- 1}
      if (j == (f[i]+1)){z[i,j] <- 1}
      if (j == (f[i]+2)){z[i,j] <- 1}
      if (j >= (f[i]+3)){z[i,j] <- 1}
      if (j >= (f[i]+4)){z[i,j] <- 2}
    }
  }
  z <- as.matrix(z)
  return(z)
}
age = recode_ch(j_ch,f.j)

###############################################################
CMR CODE
###############################################################

# Write JAGS model file
cat(file="ATPU_ZIGP.txt", "
model {
# Priors and constraints
for (i in 1:nind){
   for (t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
      logit(phi[i,t]) <- alpha[age[i,t]] + eps[age[i,t],t] # Constrain survival to be age-specific
      } #t
   } #i
   

for (u in 1:2){
   alpha[u] ~ dunif(0, 10)       # Priors for age and time specific survival
   }


for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
for (u in 1:2){
  eps[u,t] ~ dnorm(0,tau)
  }
}


# More priors
 
  epsilon ~ dgamma(1,1) # Prior for mean expected # encounters per individual
  gamma[1] ~ dbeta(1, 1)  # Prior for probability of availablity at time t given absense at time t-1
  gamma[2] ~ dbeta(1, 1) # Prior for probability of availablity at time t given available at time t-1
  sigma ~ dunif(0.5, 100)
  tau <- pow(sigma, -2)

  
 # Take inverse logit to backtransform survival probabilities
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
     phi.j[t] <- 1 / (1+exp(-alpha[1]-eps[1,t]))
     phi.a[t] <- 1 / (1+exp(-alpha[2]-eps[2,t]))
   }


###############################################################
CJS model 
###############################################################
# Capture-recapture data (CJS model with multinomial likelihood)
# Define the multinomial likelihood

# CMR Model Likelihood components
for (i in 1:nind){

   for (t in (f[i]+1):n.occasions){
   
      z[i,t] ~ dbern(phi[i,t-1] * z[i,t-1])
   
      # State process
      a[i,t] ~ dbern(mu1[i,t])
      mu1[i,t] <- z[i,t] * gamma[a[i,t-1]+1]
     
      # Observation process
      c[i,t] ~ dpois(mu2[i,t])
      mu2[i,t] <- a[i,t] * epsilon
      } #t
   } #i

} # end model

")




# Parameters monitored
parameters <- c("alpha","gamma","phi.j","phi.a", "epsilon")



inits <- function(){list(alpha = runif(2, 0, 1),
                         sigma = runif(1, 0.1, 10))}


ATPU_ZIGP_data <- list(z = z.dat,
                       a = a.dat,
                       f = f,
                       nind = dim(ch)[1],
                       n.occasions = dim(ch)[2],
                       c=c,
                       age=age)

 
# MCMC settings
ni <- 500000; nb <- 100000; nc <- 3; nt <- 3; na <- 5000

# Call JAGS
ATPU_ZIGP_out <- jags(ATPU_ZIGP_data, inits=inits, parameters, "ATPU_ZIGP.txt", n.iter=ni, n.burnin=nb, n.chains=nc, n.thin=nt, n.adapt=na, parallel = TRUE)

 

####################### END CODE ################################

Hi Michael,

I chatted briefly with Thomas and this is the solution he recommended as well. This is essentialy exactly what I am trying right now and so far so good. I knew it has to be an easy solution but my brain just couldn't envision what that would be. Thank you both so much for the help!  

Cheers,

Sarah
